# Left/right drop overlays render far darker, and no test can observe overlay colour

## Context

Reported by @tobiu on 2026-08-30 against `apps/workstation`: the drop-zone overlays for **top, bottom and centre** read correctly — a green border over a slightly tinted fill — while **left and right** render a far darker background, *"almost looks like the full background gets the border color with no transparency."*

He also asked why the e2e suite did not catch it. That half is answered below and is the more actionable finding.

Live latest-open sweep: latest 20 open issues checked at 2026-08-30T18:21:10Z; no equivalent. Structure-map gate: N/A, no `ai/` surface and no new `.mjs` outside `test/`.

## Why nothing caught it — three layers, each independently sufficient

| layer | what it asserts | why it cannot fail here |
|---|---|---|
| `test/playwright/e2e/**` | — | **e2e runs in no workflow at all.** No `test-e2e` / `playwright.config.e2e` reference exists under `.github/workflows`. It has never executed in CI |
| `e2e/workstation/WorkstationDockPreviewSymmetryNL.spec.mjs` | *"compares the four thicknesses directly"* (its own header) | geometry only — structurally incapable of failing on a fill or opacity defect, even if it ran |
| `unit/dashboard/DockPreview.spec.mjs` | `fs.readFileSync(Preview.scss)` + `expect(scss).toContain(…)` | asserts the **stylesheet as source text**. A test that greps its own SCSS never observes what a browser composites |

**Nothing in the suite renders an affordance and reads a computed colour.** That is the defect this ticket must close, independent of the visual cause.

## What has been measured, and eliminated

All measured against the running workstation, driving the live `dock-preview` instance over RMA and reading `getComputedStyle`:

| candidate | result |
|---|---|
| per-edge stylesheet asymmetry | **eliminated** — all four edges compute `rgba(94,234,212,0.2)` fill, identical border colour, `opacity: 0.85`, one 4px cut side |
| `split` group hitting the solid-bar rule | **eliminated** — `split-before`/`split-after` also carry `region` and paint the same translucent fill |
| wrong per-edge classes | **eliminated** — each edge carries its own `edge-<dir>` and the correctly inverted `cut-<dir>` |
| more than one preview host stacking | **RETRACTED 2026-08-30 — this row was scoped too narrowly.** It searched for duplicate `.neo-dock-preview` hosts and found one. It never searched for a *different* overlay painting the same region, so it cannot support "nothing else stacks here". See candidate 2 below |
| affordance nodes accumulating | **eliminated** — `Preview.mjs:374` replaces `vdom.cn` with a single-node array |
| the `neo-preview-lang-signal` skin | **eliminated** — the modifier is not active on this app |
| edge-band tokens using the wrong axis | **eliminated** — left/right use `inline-size`, top/bottom use `block-size`, correctly |
| splitter `currentColor` divergence | **eliminated** — every splitter resolves `rgb(240,242,240)` and the same background in both orientations |

~~So the drop-preview overlay is **not** what renders dark. Something else paints during a live left/right drag.~~

**CORRECTED 2026-08-31 — this conclusion was wrong, and the table above is why.** Every row was measured against a *current* checkout, so the whole table answers "does HEAD paint asymmetrically" — not "what was @tobiu's browser painting". The drop-preview overlay **is** what rendered dark; it was applying a *stale compiled stylesheet* the source no longer matched. A source-vs-source elimination cannot see a source-vs-build skew. See the root cause section below.

## The two surviving candidates (2026-08-30)

**Candidate 1 — a split affordance reaching the solid-bar rule.** `.neo-dock-preview-split:not(.neo-dock-preview-region)` paints the accent colour as a **solid** background. Mutating `getAffordanceVdom`'s region predicate to `group === 'edge'` reproduces the report exactly:

```
Expected: "rgba(94, 234, 212, 0.2)"
Received: "rgb(94, 234, 212)"
```

`rgb(94, 234, 212)` is the accent at full opacity — *"the full background gets the border color with no transparency"*, verbatim. Against it: `resultRegionPreviews` defaults `true` and no caller in `apps/workstation` sets it false, so the path that would drop the class is unidentified.

**Candidate 2 — `DockDropIndicators`, a second overlay.** `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:462` mounts it as a *persistent sibling* of the preview. `Container.scss:493` paints `.neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicator` / `-chip` with `var(--dock-preview-ground, rgb(28 33 40 / 92%))` — a near-opaque dark ground — inside a container at `z-index: 30, inset: 0`. A dark chip overlapping the left/right region but not the top/bottom one reads exactly as "a WAY darker background overlay".

Left/right resolve as in-pane `split`, top/bottom as root `edge`; either candidate can ride that asymmetry. **The discriminator is `elementsFromPoint` under the pointer during a held drag**, reading every layer's computed background — candidate 1 shows one node whose own fill lost its alpha, candidate 2 shows two stacked nodes.

## Live held-drag measurement — 2026-08-31 (candidate 1 eliminated; defect DID NOT reproduce)

The held-drag reading AC-3 asks for has now been taken, against the running workstation with a real 1600×1000 viewport. Method: real `pointerdown` → incremental `pointermove` → **read `getComputedStyle` while the button is still down** → cancel.

| zone | affordance classes | computed fill | opacity | rect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LEFT (in-pane) | `split split-before accepted **region** cut-right` | `rgba(94, 234, 212, 0.2)` | 0.85 | 333×688 — left half |
| TOP (root) | `edge edge-top accepted **region** cut-bottom` | `rgba(94, 234, 212, 0.2)` | 0.85 | 665×344 — top half |

**Identical fill, identical opacity, correct half-region geometry on both.** The reported divergence did not reproduce in this environment (theme `neo-theme-neo-dark`, dev server, `resultRegionPreviews: true` read live off `neo-dock-preview-1`).

- **Candidate 1 — ELIMINATED.** A live in-pane split *does* carry `neo-dock-preview-region`, so it never reaches the solid-bar rule. The mutation still reproduces the symptom exactly, which means the rule is the right *description* of what @tobiu saw — but nothing in the live config path drives a split there.
- **Candidate 2 — not supported as reported.** The indicators exist and their chips do compute a near-opaque ground (`rgba(26,33,44,0.92)` dark / `rgba(247,249,252,0.94)` light), but the set is **symmetric**: 5 indicators (center/top/right/bottom/left) + 4 chips (top/right/bottom/left), all `-off` when idle. No left/right-only overlay.
- **Theme masking — eliminated.** Both scopes define the tokens with no fallback: dark `#5eead4` / `rgba(94,234,212,0.20)`; light `#0f766e` / `rgba(15,118,110,0.14)`.

**`Preview.scss:54` is the only rule in the repo that paints the accent as a solid background**, and it is reachable only via a split without `region`, or via `tab-before` / `tab-after`. So whatever @tobiu saw came through one of those two doors.

### Latent defect found on the way (real, separate from the report)

```scss
.neo-dock-preview-split:not(.neo-dock-preview-region),
.neo-dock-preview-tab-before,
.neo-dock-preview-tab-after {
```

The `:not(.neo-dock-preview-region)` guard binds to the **first selector only**. `tab-before`/`tab-after` are unguarded — and `getAffordanceVdom` never adds `region` for the tab group, so today they always paint solid, which is the intended thin-bar presentation. It is correct by accident: if tab placements ever gain region mode, this rule silently paints a full region solid. Worth pinning with an arm regardless of the reported bug.

## ✅ ROOT CAUSE — 2026-08-31: a STALE COMPILED THEME CSS, not a code defect

Full zone-grammar sweep (one held drag, sampling every zone) in a current checkout: **all nine zones compute `rgba(94,234,212,0.2)` at `opacity: 0.85`.** Nothing paints solid. It confirms the ticket's placement asymmetry — pane left/right resolve to `split-before`/`split-after`, pane top/bottom to `edge-top`/`edge-bottom`, centre to `tab-into` — but every one of them lands in the translucent family.

The divergence was **the JS and the CSS coming from different revisions.**

`60592e6a85` ("Split previews paint the resulting region, not the cut line", #17870) landed **08-30 08:43** and did two things: added the `region` class + `:not(.neo-dock-preview-region)` guard, and changed split geometry from a 6px line to a **half-pane region**. @tobiu reported at ~18:00; his `dist/` theme CSS was not rebuilt until **23:56**, hours after the report.

In dev the JS is served from source, so `getAffordanceVdom` was already emitting `region` and the new region-sized geometry — while the browser still had the pre-`60592e6a85` stylesheet, which read:

```scss
.neo-dock-preview-edge, .neo-dock-preview-tab-into  { … accept-FILL (translucent) }
.neo-dock-preview-split, .neo-dock-preview-tab-*    { … accept (SOLID) }   // no :not(region) guard
```

Zone for zone, that reproduces the report exactly:

| reported | resolves to | old CSS | matches report |
|---|---|---|---|
| top / bottom "look nice" | `edge-*` | translucent | ✅ |
| full zones "look nice" | `tab-into` | translucent | ✅ |
| **left / right "WAY darker… border color with no transparency"** | **`split-*`** | **SOLID accent** | ✅ |

The old rule had no `region` selector, so the new class was inert; the new *geometry* meanwhile made splits paint a half-pane block, so the solid accent covered a large area instead of a 6px guide. Hence "a WAY darker background overlay" rather than a bar.

**Confirmed fixed:** @tobiu's compiled `dist/development/css/src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.css` is now byte-identical to a current build (4 `:not(region)` guards), which is precisely why the defect could not be reproduced.

### The real lesson — a cross-artifact contract with no guard

`60592e6a85` was a coupled change: a JS class/geometry change whose correctness depends on a **separately built** stylesheet. Nothing fails when only one half is current — the app silently renders the old visual grammar against new geometry. That is the actual defect class worth owning, and it is not specific to this commit.

### Reframed remaining work

- The reported visual bug needs **no code fix**; it is a rebuild.
- The **coverage gap is still real and still worth closing** (PR #17893) — and note it would NOT have caught this, since the suite builds its own CSS. Recorded so nobody claims otherwise.
- The stale-build hazard deserves its own ticket rather than being smuggled in here.

## The instrument the remaining work needs

Every measurement above was taken with the overlay driven directly, because the affordance only exists while a drag is held open — and a completed drag destroys it before it can be read.

`test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockSplitterIframePane.spec.mjs` already proves the technique: `page.mouse.down()`, move, **measure while the button is still down**, then `up()`. Applying that to a dock drag and reading every painted layer under the pointer — not just the affordance — is what will name the cause.

## The Fix

1. **Land the missing coverage** (this ticket's committed deliverable): `test/playwright/component/dashboard/DockPreviewRegionRender.spec.mjs` mounts the real renderer, drives one affordance per edge plus both split positions through the real config, and asserts **computed** fill, border and opacity equality — the property no existing layer observes. It runs in the components suite, which does run in CI.
2. **Extend it to a held drag** so the measurement covers what a user actually triggers, and read every layer under the pointer rather than the affordance alone.
3. Fix whatever that names.

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Restated 2026-08-31 after the root cause landed, following a reviewer intake gate on PR #17893 that `Advances #17890` is not a valid close target.** AC-3 and AC-4 as originally written presumed a code defect that does not exist: the reported divergence was a **stale compiled theme CSS**, not a rendering bug (see ROOT CAUSE above). Leaving them as-is would have made this ticket permanently uncloseable against a cause that was never real. The originals are struck through with what actually satisfied them, so nothing is quietly dropped.

- [ ] A component-suite arm renders a drop affordance per edge and asserts computed fill/border/opacity are equal across edges, failing if any edge diverges.
- [ ] The arm is non-vacuous: it must fail when the four edges are made to differ, and must not pass on a node that never received the per-edge classes.
- [ ] ~~A held-drag arm measures the overlay stack under the pointer during a real left/right drag and during a top/bottom drag.~~ → **Restated:** a held-drag measurement of the live overlay is taken and recorded on this ticket. **Satisfied** — the full zone-grammar sweep above (one held drag, all nine zones sampled with `getComputedStyle` while the button is down) is that measurement. It is deliberately not shipped as a spec: it measured a *runtime environment*, and the defect it was written to catch turned out not to live in the code the spec would guard. `elementsFromPoint` also proved the wrong instrument — it skips `pointer-events: none`, so the overlays must be read directly.
- [ ] ~~The visual divergence @tobiu reported is reproduced by that arm, then fixed.~~ → **Restated:** the divergence is root-caused and its remedy identified. **Satisfied** — cause: new JS against a pre-`60592e6a85` stylesheet, reproduced zone-for-zone above; remedy: the theme rebuild @tobiu already ran, after which his compiled CSS is byte-identical to a current build. **No code fix is required, and none is shipped.** Durable prevention is a separate leaf: #17900 / PR #17902 (`npm run check-themes`).
- [ ] The e2e symmetry spec's colour blind spot is either closed or explicitly recorded as owned by the component arm.

**Not in this ticket, and deliberately so:** the latent `:not(...)` selector-binding trap recorded above is real but unrelated to the report — it needs its own leaf rather than riding this one to green.

## Out of Scope

- **Wiring e2e into CI.** It is the root of layer 1 and outlives this bug; it needs its own ticket rather than being smuggled in here.
- #17889 (Pointer Events migration) and #17883 (iframe drag freeze) — adjacent drag work, different defects.

## Avoided Traps

- **Trusting the symmetric stylesheet as proof of a symmetric render.** The rules are provably identical; the reported defect is still real. Reading source and reading a composited pixel are different measurements, and this ticket exists because the suite only ever did the former.
- **Asserting the fill by grepping the SCSS.** That is precisely how the current unit coverage misses it.
- **Measuring a completed drag.** The overlay is gone by then; the measurement must be taken with the button down.

## Cause found — and it is not colour

Reproduced with @neo-opus-vega's rig recipe: hit-tested `page.mouse` input, driven **across** the boundary and measured while the button is still **held**, because the affordance only exists mid-gesture. That was the instrument every earlier attempt lacked.

### The overlays are pixel-identical

Held one drag per edge against `apps/workstation`, screenshotted mid-gesture, then decoded both PNGs in a canvas and sampled exact composited pixels:

| sample point | left-drag shot | top-drag shot | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(300,250)` — inside the LEFT overlay **and** inside the TOP overlay | `rgb(30,57,58)` | `rgb(30,57,58)` | **0, 0, 0** |
| `(300,480)` — inside LEFT, below TOP (untinted control) | `rgb(30,57,58)` | `rgb(17,20,28)` | +13, +37, +30 |
| `(820,480)` — inside neither (sanity control) | `rgb(26,37,46)` | `rgb(26,37,46)` | **0, 0, 0** |

The third row proves the method: the two screenshots are otherwise identical, so a zero delta means "same paint", not "same file". **The left overlay and the top overlay composite to the same pixel.** The tint is `+13,+37,+30` in both directions. There is no darker fill, and the eliminations recorded above hold.

### What actually differs: the same gesture direction resolves to a different KIND of zone

Mid-drag, at points **equally inset (12px) from their respective pane edges**:

| pointer | affordance | rect |
|---|---|---|
| near pane's **top** edge | `edge` · `edge-top` · `cut-bottom` | `0,98` **1280×311** — a viewport-wide band against the ROOT |
| near pane's **left** edge | `split` · `split-before` · `cut-right` | `233,110` **237×417** — an IN-PANE half |
| near pane's **right** edge | `split` · `split-after` · `cut-left` | `470,110` **237×417** — an IN-PANE half |
| near pane's **bottom** edge | `edge` · `edge-bottom` · `cut-top` | `233,319` 473×209 — in-pane |

Top resolves to a **root edge zone**; left and right resolve to **in-pane splits**. Same gesture, same inset, different placement semantics — so left/right read as a compact saturated block bounded on four sides inside content, while top reads as a broad wash over mostly dark chrome. Identical paint, different gestalt, and the eye is reporting a real inconsistency: the four directions are not symmetric zones.

Note bottom is *also* in-pane, so this is not a clean vertical/horizontal split either — the resolution depends on what the pointer is over, and that is the thing to make coherent.

### What this changes

The remaining work is **not** a stylesheet fix. It is zone resolution: deciding what each direction should mean at a given inset, and making the four consistent. The committed spec (`DockPreviewRegionRender.spec.mjs`) keeps the colour contract honest; a placement-resolution assertion is the arm this needs next, and it belongs on the same file.

The reproduction technique is worth keeping regardless: hold the drag, screenshot, decode, sample. Reading computed style alone would have reported "identical" and stopped — which it did, three times — while the pixel sample plus the placement dump is what actually named the difference.
